**Naming of the Surah**

• It is called al-Fath (The Victory), because it opens with the good tidings of a victory for the believers, a mighty triumph, and establishment in the land. The mention of "al-Fath" recurs in several places in the surah.

**Some of the Objectives of the Surah**

• Glad tidings to the believers of the good outcome of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, and that it is a victory and a conquest in which tranquility (al-sakinah) descended into the hearts of the believers. God informed them that the final outcome is theirs, and that the circle of evil falls upon the polytheists and the hypocrites.

• A demonstration of God's protection of His sincere allies when they were called to jihad, and how they hastened to pledge allegiance (bay'ah) to the Prophet ﷺ for fighting. God protected them and did not give the Meccan disbelievers power over them, just as His gentleness—glorified is He—was manifest toward His oppressed servants in Mecca, since God had not permitted the Muslims to fight the polytheists at that time, in order to safeguard those oppressed people.

• A censure of those who stayed behind from going out with the Messenger of God ﷺ to Mecca, thinking that the Messenger ﷺ and the believers would never return. God frustrated them by returning the Messenger ﷺ and the believers to Medina, whom He honored with this conquest, and He promised them a near victory over the Jews of Khaybar.

• Praise of the believers who followed the Prophet ﷺ in hardship and ease, an explanation of a number of the believers' qualities, an exhortation to them to adopt these qualities, a demonstration of their effect on their conduct, and God's honoring them with forgiveness and a great reward.

**[Tafsir]**

Indeed We have granted you, O Messenger, a manifest victory (fathan mubinan), in which God makes your religion prevail and grants you victory over your enemy. It is the truce of al-Hudaybiyah, through which people became secure from one another, so the circle of the call to God's religion widened, and whoever wished to stand upon the reality of Islam could come to know it. Thus people entered God's religion in multitudes during that period; for this reason God called it a manifest victory, meaning clear and evident.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 48, verses 2–3:

We have granted you a clear victory, and We have made it easy for you; so that Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins, because of what came about from this conquest of great acts of obedience and because of the hardships you bore; and that He may complete His favour upon you by making your religion prevail and by granting you victory over your enemies; and that He may guide you to a straight path of religion with no crookedness in it; and that Allah may help you with a mighty help through which Islam will not be weakened.

It is He who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers, in belief in Allah and His Messenger, on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyya, so they were settled and certainty took firm root in them, that they might increase in faith in Allah and in following His Messenger, along with their existing faith and obedience. To Allah, glorified and exalted, belong the armies of the heavens and the earth, and with them He grants victory to His believing servants. Allah has always been All-Knowing of the interests of His creation, All-Wise in His management and His handiwork.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 48, verse 5:

God will admit the believing men and the believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, and He will remove from them their evil deeds, so He will not punish them for them. That reward with God is deliverance from every distress and triumph in obtaining every desired thing.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 48, verse 6:

And Allah will punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women, who assume a wrong assumption about Allah, that He will not grant victory to His Prophet and the believers with him over their enemies, and that He will not make His religion prevail. Upon them is the turn of misfortune and everything that displeases them; and Allah's anger is upon them, and He has expelled them from His mercy, and He has prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination to which they will go.

To Allah, glorified and exalted is He, belong the armies of the heavens and the earth. He strengthens His believing servants with them. And Allah is Mighty over His creation, Wise in the management of their affairs.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 48, verses 8–9:

Indeed, We have sent you, O Messenger, as a witness over your nation, testifying to their conveyance of the message; as a bringer of glad tidings to those who obey you, of Paradise; and as a warner to those who disobey you, of immediate and deferred punishment; so that you [believers] may believe in Allah and His Messenger, support Allah by supporting His religion, venerate Allah, and glorify Him at the beginning and end of the day.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 48, verse 10:

Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, O Prophet, at al-Hudaybiyah, to fight, are in fact pledging allegiance to Allah. They make the covenant with Him, seeking His Paradise and His good pleasure. ﴿The hand of Allah is above their hands.﴾ So He is with them: He hears their words, sees their place, and knows their inner thoughts and outward actions. Whoever breaks his pledge, the harm of that falls only upon himself. And whoever fulfills what he covenanted with Allah, by being steadfast when meeting the enemy in the cause of Allah and supporting His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), Allah will give him a great reward, which is Paradise. In this verse is an affirmation of the attribute of the Hand for Allah, Exalted is He, in a manner befitting Him, without likening Him to creation and without specifying its modality.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 48, verse 11:

The Bedouins who lagged behind you, O Prophet, from setting out with you to Makkah will say, when you rebuke them: "Our wealth and our families kept us busy, so ask your Lord to forgive us for our lagging behind." They say this with their tongues, but there is no reality to it in their hearts. Say to them: "Who can avail you anything from God if He wills harm for you or wills benefit for you?" The matter is not as these hypocrites supposed, that God does not know what their inner selves conceal of hypocrisy. Rather, He, glory be to Him, is ever Acquainted with what they do; nothing of the deeds of His creatures is hidden from Him.

Rather, the matter is not as you claimed, that you were preoccupied with your wealth and your families. Instead, you thought that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and those with him of his Companions would perish and would never return to you, and Satan made that appealing in your hearts. You also harbored a wicked assumption, thinking that Allah would not grant victory to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions over their enemies. And you were a people doomed to ruin, with no good in you.

Whoever does not believe in Allah and in what His Messenger ﷺ brought, and does not act according to His law, then he is a disbeliever deserving of punishment. Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers the torment of the Blaze in the Fire.

To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. He pardons by His mercy whom He wills, concealing his sin, and He punishes by His justice whom He wills. And Allah, glorified and exalted, has always been Forgiving to whoever repents to Him, Merciful toward him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 48, verse 15:

The ones left behind will say, when you (O Prophet) and your companions set out to take the spoils of Khaybar which Allah promised you: "Let us follow you." They want to change Allah's promise to you by this. Say to them: "You will not follow us to Khaybar, for Allah the Exalted said to us before our return to al-Madinah: 'The spoils of Khaybar belong only to those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah with you.'" They will say: "It is not as you say; Allah did not command you with this. Rather, you prevent us from going out with you out of envy, so that we do not share the spoils with you." But it is not as they claim; rather, they did not comprehend of Allah, concerning what is for them and against them in matters of religion, except a little.

Say to the Bedouin Arabs who stayed behind (they being the desert dwellers) from fighting: "You will be called to fight a people of great might in battle; you will either fight them, or they will submit without fighting. So if you obey Allah in what He calls you to of fighting these people, He will give you Paradise; but if you disobey Him, as you did when you stayed behind from marching with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Makkah, He will punish you with a painful punishment."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 48, verse 17:

There is no blame upon the blind among you, O people, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, for staying behind from jihad with the believers, because of their inability. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, beneath their palaces and trees; and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, staying behind from jihad with the believers, He will punish him with a painful, agonizing punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 48, verses 18–19:

Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, O Prophet, under the tree—and this is the Pledge of Ridwan (Bay'at al-Ridwan) at al-Hudaybiyah—so Allah knew what was in the hearts of these believers of faith, sincerity and loyalty. So Allah sent down tranquility upon them and made their hearts firm, and He compensated them for what they had missed through the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah with a near victory, which is the conquest of Khaybar, and abundant spoils that they would take from the wealth of the Jews of Khaybar. And Allah is Mighty in His retribution against His enemies, Wise in the management of the affairs of His creation.

God has promised you many spoils that you will take, and He has hastened for you this (portion): the spoils of Khaybar. He restrained the hands of people from you, so that no harm befell you, though your enemies had intended to fight you and to reach those you left behind in Madinah. This was so that (your) defeat of them, your safety and your booty might be a sign by which you take heed, and by which you may infer that Allah is your Protector and Helper, and that He guides you to a straight path with no crookedness in it. Allah has also promised you another spoil that you have not been able to obtain, though Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is capable of it; it lies under His management and dominion, and He has promised it to you, and what He promised must certainly come to pass. And Allah is ever Able over all things, nothing can overpower Him. Had the disbelievers of Quraysh fought you at Makkah, they would have fled from you, turning their backs to you as the defeated one does in battle; then they would find neither a protector besides Allah to take their side in fighting you, nor a helper to assist them in fighting you.

The way of God which He has established among His creation from before: granting victory to His soldiers and defeating His enemies. And you will not find, O Prophet, any change in the way of God.

He it is who restrained the hands of the polytheists from you, and your hands from them, in al-Hudaybiyyah (a place west of Makkah), after you had gained power over them, so that they came under your authority. These polytheists are the ones who went out against the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Hudaybiyyah. The Muslims seized them, then released them and did not kill them. They numbered about eighty men. And Allah is ever Seeing of your deeds, nothing hidden from Him.

The Quraysh disbelievers are those who denied Allah's Oneness, and who barred you on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah from entering the Sacred Mosque, and prevented the sacrificial animals, and held them back from reaching their place of sacrifice, which is the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram). Had it not been for believing men who were oppressed and believing women living among these disbelievers in Makkah, concealing their faith out of fear for themselves, whom you did not know, lest you trample them with your army and thereby kill them, so that there would befall you through that killing a sin, a disgrace, and a blood-money payment without knowledge, We would have given you power over the polytheists. [This was so] that Allah might admit into His mercy whom He wills, and bestow upon them faith after disbelief. Had those believing men and women been distinguished from the polytheists of Makkah and come out from among them, We would have punished those among them who disbelieved and denied with a painful, agonizing punishment.

When those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam), so as not to acknowledge the message of Muhammad (ﷺ). Among this was their refusal to write "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" in the treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah, and they refused to write "This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, agreed to." So Allah sent down tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers with him, and obliged them to the words "There is no god but Allah," which are the foundation of all piety. The Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers with him had more right to the word of piety than the polytheists, and they were also its people rather than the polytheists. And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing, nothing being hidden from Him.

Certainly God has fulfilled the vision for His Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), truly. He saw it: "You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque of God, secure, not fearing anyone, with your heads shaved and your hair trimmed," and God knew the good and the benefit in turning you away from Makkah that year and in your entering it later, which you did not know. So God made, in place of your entering Makkah which you had been promised, a near victory: the truce of al-Hudaybiyyah and the conquest of Khaybar.

It is He who sent His Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), with clear guidance and the religion of Islam, so that He may make it prevail over all other religions. And sufficient is Allah as a witness, O Messenger, that He is your helper and the one who makes your religion triumph over every other religion.

Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those with him are firm against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah in their prayers, hoping that their Lord will show them favor, admit them to Paradise, and be pleased with them. The mark of their obedience to Allah is apparent in their faces, from the trace of prostration and worship. This is their description in the Torah. Their description in the Gospel is like that of a seed that sent out its shoot and its sprout; then its branches multiplied, it grew strong, and it stood firm upon its stalks, beautiful in appearance, pleasing the farmers. [This is so] that He may enrage the disbelievers by these believers in their multitude and the beauty of their appearance.

In this is evidence of the disbelief of one who hates the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), because whoever is enraged by the Companions, the cause of rage, which is disbelief, is found in him. Allah has promised those among them who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did what Allah commanded them and avoided what He forbade them forgiveness for their sins and a great reward that never ends, which is Paradise. Allah's promise is true and affirmed, and it is never broken. Whoever follows the footsteps of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) is, in ruling, in deserving forgiveness and a great reward, like them. They have the virtue, the precedence, and the perfection in which no one from this Ummah can equal them. May Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased.
